context:
The walkthrough you asked for:
- What it was: in October, each tool call on Windows started about 6 bash and 2 python processes per hook. #551 holds tests for 'if' filters, so a hook such as ste_gate (the plain-English check) only starts when a matching file type is edited.
- What happened: on Oct 21 a Windows probe found the filters unreliable. Paths with backslashes never match, matching is case-sensitive, and a miss silently skips the check. You ruled: filter only config_watch, on exact file names, and park the ste_gate and prose_judge filters.
- Now: c19 (start fewer processes per tool call) shipped that and is done. #551 is the leftover draft for the parked part, untouched since.
Closing it loses nothing: the branch stays and the PR can be reopened if the parked filters come back.

options.how: The build advisor closes #551 with a note pointing to c19's ruling; the branch stays for a reopen.
options.label: Close it, branch kept

ref: PR #551 (settings: if filters so idle hooks start no shell), step c19
title: Close the stale draft PR #551
why: Your own ruling parked this work.
